map_role: Dry impact-caldera dispatch and broken freight crossing, with upper bridge-fracture flight and an underground recovery bypass
macro_topology: crater with dense edge-anchored loading settlements, a deliberately discontinuous aerial bridge, an open bowl and nested bedrock service cavities
density_profile: Two industrial rim clusters and fragmented span supports bound a broad navigable negative-space caldera, with distinct compact underfloor workrooms

route_grammar.primary: West rim start → upper west sky → broken-girder fracture aperture → crater drop → east capture → west floor return → finish
route_grammar.alternative: West rim start → cableway holdout → sloping west entry → underbridge caldera basin → east catcher
route_grammar.blockage: A genuine 70×86-cell wall across the central fracture eliminates its literal checkpoint while retaining the lower bypass and finish

interesting_relationships: A surviving high tension arch roots the split bridge without rebuilding the absent deck
Flight clearance and geological bowl profile are distinct from the sparse overhead visual machinery
An intentional west shaft and below-cable passage keep recovery possible when the bridge fracture closes
Entered below-floor bays remain physically accessible from the open basin
authoring_affordances: Wide crater sky and floor remain available for later human-authored spacecraft or encounter geometry
Two interrupted bridge ends are prepared as an optional destruction/reconnection worksite
Underfloor service bays can be extended into additional cave branches without disturbing the race loop
East freighter workface offers an unused crane/event rigging location

setpiece_candidates.staging: The still-open fracture lies below the tension arch; the low bypass remains reachable
A descending cableway shoulder provides a midcourse diversion and recovery entrance
Open ground beneath the freight claw allows later moving cargo and actor encounters
An empty bedrock service cavity has room for a future modular sublevel

procedural_exemplar_value: Demonstrates a dry geological basin carrying split suspended bridge hardware across a large negative-space racing well, with independently enterable below-grade service cavities and alternate west-rooted bypasses; useful as an example-derived mixed geological/engineering parts grammar.
similarity_avoidance: Unlike the recent compact industrial racers with evenly spaced ceiling/floor capacitors, horizontal double flight tubes, annuli or repeating ratchet gates, this map is a largely open excavated crater with asymmetric rim loading clusters and a genuinely interrupted suspended bridge, not a factory corridor.
